Elena Park: FYI onboarding Omega-13B (Llama->Gemma layout). After int4 quant + proj-swap we see a reproducible 'anglephase shimmer' around token 45 that produces small coherence loss on long summaries.
Noel Rivera: Can you paste the convert cmd and a tiny diff?
Elena Park: cmd: `python convert.py --src llama-omega13b.ckpt --dst gemma/omega13b.onnx --proj-swap --quant int4 --export-tokenizer`
Diff: fp16: '...the findings were consistent across regions.'
int4: '...the findings were consistent across regions.' (odd control-like char, phase blip near token 45)
Sasha Ivanov: Control char points to tokenizer export/normalization. Also proj-swap can permute head groups so rotary angle table must be remapped. Which quant calibration did you use? Per-head?
Elena Park: Per-head asymmetric scales from the usual cal run. Quick experiments: `--preserve-tokenizer` removes the control char, `--no-proj-swap` removes the phase shimmer. So two separate issues.
Maya Chen: That matches past cases: (1) enforce NFKC on tokenizer export and include checksum in metadata, (2) remap rotary angle buffers + per-head scale arrays in converter when doing any head permute/proj-swap, and (3) add a loader-time head-order checksum that can auto-remap at load if mismatch detected.
Noel Rivera: For int4 specifically, small scale misalignments amplify phase errors. Suggest a short calibration pass that computes head_scale_correction and an optional `--apply-head-correction` to slightly nudge rotary angles pre-quant. Cheap and can be a fallback while remap lands.
Elena Park: I'll prototype remap + optional head correction. Will add a smoke test: 20 punctuation-heavy prompts, compare token diffs and KV-cache cosine at t=60 against fp16.
ci-bot: test/omega-rotary-shadowwalk queued: 0/20 run so far.
